commit.subject: refactor(steme): colocate the baseline register with its unit and drop --baseline
commit.body:
The baseline register moves from one repo-root steme-baseline.json to a
per-unit <unit>/steme.baseline.json, derived from the audit target the
invocation already supplies — and takes the manifest's naming family
(steme.package.json / steme.baseline.json) now that the two are siblings.
Nothing needs a flag to find it anymore, so --baseline is removed from audit,
baseline write, and baseline accept-drift; stale invocations fail loudly as
unknown options. The missing-register refusal stops naming an override that no
longer exists, and the inert-flag refusal is deleted with its subject.

Entry keying is deliberately frozen: entries still carry repo-relative paths
and fingerprints, and splitEntriesForApp still partitions per unit — that flips
in the next commit, where a reviewer can see it in isolation. The E2E suites
drop ~46 --baseline call sites that existed only to isolate a register per
fixture; the derived location makes tmpdir fixtures hermetic for free.
steme.usage.kdl and docs/cli.md are regenerated.

phases.title: Colocate and rename the register; remove --baseline

commit.subject: feat(steme): key baseline entries unit-relative; one register, one unit
commit.body:
Baseline entries are now keyed relative to the unit root: the entry file and
the fingerprint's two path inputs come straight from the violation's edge
(src/core/a.ts), not from posix.join(appRelPath, …). Accepted debt therefore
survives renaming or moving the unit — proven by a lifecycle scenario that
seeds a register, renames the unit directory, and audits the new path: red
(exit 1, all drift new) under repo-relative keying, green (exit 0, all known)
under unit-relative keying. An in-place audit passes under both designs, which
is why the test moves the unit.

The fingerprint prefix stays v1: per the pre-ship versioning policy — the
recipe is redefined in place, registers are regenerated rather than migrated,
and the fingerprint comment that mandated a v2: bump is rewritten to state the
recipe and the policy instead of contradicting it.

A one-unit register has nothing to partition: splitEntriesForApp and the
otherEntries thread-through are deleted, the governance read drops its
appRelPath parameter, and silent preservation of foreign entries is replaced
by a refusal — a register holding an entry whose file escapes the unit
(absolute, or normalizing to ../) exits 2 naming the entry, from all three
register-reading flows. The foreign-entries lifecycle scenario is deleted as
unrepresentable and replaced by the refusal scenario. Drift classification
compares entries against the diagnostic's unit-relative file; diagnostics keep
their repo-relative file for reporting.

phases.title: Unit-relative entry identity; a register describes exactly one unit
